resources.string: Makes one press of Back close the keyboard and go back, and keeps the touchpad on the keys when a notification shows. At a few moments, such as while the Sym panel is open, it sees the keys you press. It can\'t read your screen, and it doesn\'t keep or send anything.
The words are imported, but the favourites couldn\'t be kept. Try again.
Copy something and it shows up here for an hour.
To pin a clip, press Enter, then the key under it.
Press the key under a clip to pin or unpin it
Press Backspace or Clear again. Pinned clips stay.

Clipboard. What you copied in the last hour, and the clips you pinned. Press the key under a clip to paste it. Swipe up or down on the keys for more, and left or right for Pinned. Enter pins, Backspace clears, and Alt goes back.
Older clips: press Sym, then A
To use names from your contacts, allow Contacts for TitanKeys here.

resources.string: TitanKeys uses Android\'s Accessibility service for three things. It\'s optional.
Back: one press closes the keyboard and goes back.
Keys: at a few moments, it sees which keys you press before the app does.
Touchpad: it keeps the touchpad on the keys when a notification pops up.
It can\'t read your screen, and it doesn\'t keep or send anything it sees.
Say no and TitanKeys still types and swipes. Back may take two presses. You can turn it on later in Settings > Setup.
It sees which keys you press only at these moments:
while the Sym panel is open, so Enter and Backspace turn its pages instead of reaching the app;
in Smart Launcher\'s search field, where Smart Launcher would take your keys first, so TitanKeys types there as in any other app;
for a moment after you press Back, so your next press of Back reaches the app.
The keys are used on your phone straight away, then forgotten. It never sees the text in your apps.
